## Essential Problem:

The essential problem is the environmental impact of palm oil production, specifically deforestation, forest fires, and biodiversity loss. The user wants to understand the environmental friendliness of certified organic palm oil compared to RSPO-certified and non-certified palm oil. 

## Relevant Information:

* **Palm oil production and its environmental impact:** Palm oil is a versatile and widely used vegetable oil, but its production has been linked to deforestation, habitat loss, and greenhouse gas emissions. 
* **RSPO certification:** The Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) is a set of environmental and social standards for the sustainable production of palm oil. While not perfect, RSPO certification is generally considered better than non-certified palm oil.
* **Organic certification:** Organic certification in the EU ensures that the palm oil is produced without synthetic pesticides, fertilizers, or genetically modified organisms (GMOs). However, organic certification does not guarantee sustainability in terms of deforestation or biodiversity loss.

## Comparing Different Types of Palm Oil:

**1. Non-certified palm oil:** This is the least environmentally friendly option, as it has no guarantee of sustainable production practices. 

**2. RSPO-certified palm oil:** This is a step up from non-certified palm oil, as it adheres to some environmental and social standards. However, the RSPO has been criticized for its lack of effectiveness in preventing deforestation and human rights abuses.

**3. Certified organic palm oil:** This type of palm oil meets the EU's organic standards, which means it is produced without harmful chemicals. However, organic certification does not guarantee that the palm oil is deforestation-free or produced in a way that protects biodiversity. 

**Therefore, while certified organic palm oil might be better than non-certified palm oil in terms of chemical use, it is not necessarily a more sustainable option when it comes to deforestation and biodiversity loss.**

## Additional Considerations:

* **Traceability:** When choosing palm oil products, it is important to look for products with traceable supply chains. This allows consumers to know where the palm oil comes from and how it was produced.
* **Alternatives:** Whenever possible, it is best to avoid palm oil altogether and opt for alternative vegetable oils with lower environmental impacts, such as sunflower oil or rapeseed oil.

## Conclusion:

While certified organic palm oil might be a better choice than non-certified palm oil in some aspects, it is important to remember that it is not a guarantee of sustainability. Consumers should look for products with traceable supply chains and consider alternative oils whenever possible to minimize their environmental impact.

I recently found more information about this, so I'll self-answer. While
pesticide can have a big impact on the environment, the biggest problem with
palm oil seems to be the clearing of rainforests.

##  Organic label

[ This webpage ](https://www.rainforest-rescue.org/topics/palm-oil/questions-
and-answers#start) says:

> While organic farming prohibits the use of pesticides, chemical fertilizers
> and genetic engineering, organic labels do not establish standards against
> rainforest destruction and land grabbing. Furthermore, vast industrial
> monocultures – including those that fulfill organic production standards –
> can hardly be deemed environmentally sound.

and as an example they say that

> Agro Palma – the largest palm oil producer in Brazil – states that it
> operates 39,000 hectares of oil palm plantations on former rainforest land
> in the state of Pará in the Amazon. Its certified organic palm oil is
> produced on the 4,107-hectare Hacienda CPA

This implies that forests have been cleared for organic palm plantations. Of
course this is only 1 viewpoint, but I haven't been able to find any other
sources that backup or refute the claims that are made. So it seems LShaver is
correct with [ his comment
](https://sustainability.stackexchange.com/questions/5727/how-environmentally-
friendly-is-palm-oil-with-a-certified-organic-label#comment8002_5727) that
**organic-certified palm oil is no guarantee for a sustainable, low-
environmental impact product** .

##  RSPO label

The same article also says that the [ RSPO label
](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roundtable_on_Sustainable_Palm_Oil) is hardly
a guarantee either;

> The RSPO does not rule out the clearing of rainforest. Only primary and
> “high conservation value” (HCV) forests have been considered off-limits for
> palm oil plantations under the label since November 2005. An internationally
> recognized definition of HCV areas has not been established, however, and
> the transitions between primary and secondary rainforests are blurred in
> practice.

##  Rainforest Alliance label

[ The Rainforest Alliance says ](https://www.rainforest-
alliance.org/articles/rainforest-alliance-certified-palm-oil) that

> the clearing of natural forests is forbidden on Rainforest Alliance
> Certified oil palm plantations, which helps to protect the habitat of
> endangered wildlife such as orangutans. And farmers we work with who once
> relied on harmful pesticides and chemicals are now reducing or eliminating
> these harmful substances and replacing them with ecologically sound
> alternatives.

[ This treehugger blog ](https://www.treehugger.com/corporate-
responsibility/what-does-rainforest-alliance-certification-mean-palm-oil.html)
confirms the above. I haven't been able to find any reports that say that for
palm oil Rainforest Alliance does not live up to their claims, so it looks
like a Rainforest Alliance label is best of the 3 labels from an overall-
sustainability point of view.

**Note:** Boycotting palm oil all together is not a solution because companies
would need to switch to alternative oils which will require more agricultural
land for an equivalent yield (see also [
https://www.huiledepalmedurable.org/le-boycott-est-il-la-solution/?lang=en
](https://www.huiledepalmedurable.org/le-boycott-est-il-la-solution/?lang=en)
)
